networkAccess.reasoning: Plumb pairs the plugin with a local MCP server running on the same machine (127.0.0.1, on one of ports 31337–31346). The WebSocket carries the control channel (which screens to read/build, which assets to export); the HTTP channel carries binary uploads (screenshots and exported icons/images) and inbound asset GETs (bytes for the build path) so they never have to be base64-encoded over the WebSocket. No request ever leaves the user's machine. No analytics, no third-party endpoints. The MCP server it talks to is open source: https://github.com/tathagat22/plumb-mcp.
